bluf: Online Solutions Group is a founder led Munich search agency (founded 2008) selling SEO, GEO and Google Ads at fixed monthly prices with monthly cancellation, paired with its own Performance Suite automation and a daily AI visibility tool. The record shows a large publishing machine, 7,398 sitemap URLs with 1,175 updated in 90 days and a 605k character llms.txt, and LinkedIn video ads claiming about 80% lower costs through AI. Horus reads it Favored at 20.7; Monsoon reads Onshore wind at 55.9 with an onshore delivery claim observed. What a rival should know: it names not one client in its record, and its Google ad presence could not be checked.
doing:
The positioning line, "Munich search agency selling SEO, GEO and Google Ads at fixed prices with monthly cancellation, pairing experts with its own automation tools," decodes to a productised, low commitment search offer: a price list, exit any month, and in house software said to make the work cheaper. The headline claim, "1,000+ projects since 2008, BVDW certification for SEO and SEA, and live visibility into what budgets deliver," is quoted as a claim; no named client backs the project count.

The sold mix leads with three lines scored 3. AI Search / GEO: the title and meta name GEO, a four tier LLMO package page runs from Basic to Ultimate with daily AI monitoring. Paid Search: the title and meta include SEA and Google Ads, one of three core disciplines. SEO: the title and H1 lead with fixed price SEO and the nav lists about 15 SEO lines from B2B to Shopware. AI Automation / Agents scores 2: the homepage pairs experts with Performance Suite automation, and its own ads claim about 80% lower costs. B2B & ABM, CRO, Content, Data & Measurement, Local and Paid Social score 1; the rest score 0. Proprietary lines: the Performance Suite tool platform, an in house AI visibility tool measuring ChatGPT and LLM mentions daily, and free SEO, keyword, backlink and load time checks; no partner is listed.

Its AI posture is GEO packages sold with the daily AI visibility tool, and AI plus in house automation pitched as the route to cheaper, faster SEO; the read still marks P1 partial, since no audited citation share product shows.

The record lists no dated move, news, case study or job posting. Pricing signals: fixed monthly prices with monthly cancellation, four LLMO tiers priced net per month (figures not captured), a free potential check and tool account (P5 making). Absent for an agency claiming 1,000+ projects: any named client, case study or headcount.
clients:
The ICP is mixed; the verticals on record are B2B and ecommerce; the home market is Germany, with Munich the only office listed.

The record names no client at all: the need read stands at 0 clients, 0 observed, 0 named only, so nothing in the book can be coded or contested by name. That silence sits against a homepage claim of 1,000+ projects since 2008 and a nav that lists about 15 SEO lines, so the record shows who it sells to only through its product lines: B2B SEO, E-Commerce SEO, Enterprise SEO, Local SEO, International, and Shopware among the platforms named. Its own LinkedIn line, that many companies work with agencies that no longer deliver what they promise, positions it against incumbent agencies.

What this unnamed base needs next is inferred from the sold mix and the edition. It leads with SEO, GEO and Google Ads at fixed prices, so the inferred needs are organic demand, AI and automation and paid performance, said as an inference. KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) is the judgment the read places it best for, driven by AI Search / GEO with Paid Search adding, so buyers of the LLMO tiers will likely ask for the daily AI visibility tool to become an audited citation number, which the read says it is not yet (moderate confidence, no client evidence). KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) is its exposure, driven by Paid Search and Paid Social scored 3 and 1, so Google Ads clients on monthly cancellation likely test whether platform automation makes the fixed fee unnecessary.
house: Say and do: both testable lines are corroborated, a say/do integrity of 100. AI Search / GEO is corroborated: it publishes an llms.txt of 605k characters and holds 22 AI topic URLs; no AI crawlers are listed as blocked. Publishing cadence is corroborated at scale: 7,398 sitemap URLs including 4,706 blog pages, 1,175 updated in 90 days and 1,270 in 365. Paid Search is unknown: the Transparency Center lookup was blocked, so the record cannot say whether it runs Google ads of its own. LinkedIn shows 3 company video ads contrasting its AI backed service with agencies that underdeliver, one reading "Wir kombinieren langjährige Expertise mit KI, für ca. 80% geringere Kosten". The Radar flagged no gap. The tag stack is gtm and hotjar on WordPress; no social pixels, test tools or ABM stack show, which sits oddly beside a Usability line and a claim of live visibility into what budgets deliver.
market:

Best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), net 0.36, driven by AI Search / GEO and Paid Search. Most exposed to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer), net 0.206 against, on Paid Search and Paid Social. Best fit: The Bazaar of Agents, 44/100. Moves: making P5 (productised pricing); partial on P1, P4 and P6 (audited AI visibility, inputs for automation, agent operators); absent on P2, P3, P7 and P8 (feeds and entities, LSAs, owned audiences, ads inside assistants).

Monsoon reads 55.9, band Onshore wind: migration 56.9 against displacement 54.9. The sold mix supplies 57 of the index, SEO (16) and Paid Search (11) the most movable hours, automation overlapping 23%; the work would go 55% to Eastern Europe and 35% to South and Southeast Asia. The evidence class is observed: it claims onshore delivery in its own words through the in house tool platform; an outcome pricing term takes 5 off; no hub office is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is the empty book behind the 1,000+ projects claim: the record names no client and no case study, so a rival that brings named, described German B2B or ecommerce results to the same buyer very likely wins the proof comparison (high confidence on the observation, moderate on the win). The falsifier: a populated references section with named clients at the next compile.

Second, the in house claim: it sells mostly movable SEO and paid search hours while claiming in house tools and delivery, and its ads promise about 80% lower costs through AI, so a rival with transparent delivery can likely turn that claim into a question it has to answer.

Third, the platform exposure: KJ4 is its headwind on paid search and paid social, P4 is partial and P8 is absent, so a rival that shows results from ads inside assistants and supplies the inputs automation runs on likely takes the Google Ads line, since monthly cancellation lowers the cost of switching. It can answer on price in public, so a rate attack alone is unlikely to work (displacement 54.9).

I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and any pricing below $20 CPM would signal supply outrunning demand under KJ2, its second tailwind, and bear on its Google Ads line.

I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would test whether its fixed price model still stands apart.

The record lists no dated move to follow up; the next Radar compile (the dossier is only as fresh as 2026-09-28) should retry the blocked Transparency Center lookup, capture the LLMO tier prices and check whether a named client appears.
